rationale: The buyer is specific and named — engineering managers and CTOs at SMBs already paying for ChatGPT Team/Enterprise and Codex API, meaning they have budget authority and an active pain triggered by OpenAI's forced allowance consolidation. Willingness to pay is credible because these teams already pay $30–100+/seat and spend-visibility tools (e.g., CloudHealth, Datadog cost modules) are established paid categories. Delivery is fully automatable: a Claude-orchestrated dashboard that polls the OpenAI usage API, applies per-product budget rules, and fires alerts requires no per-customer human work after onboarding.
solution_plan: WHAT: A lightweight OpenAI spend-monitoring micro-service that splits usage by product (ChatGPT vs Codex vs other), sets per-product budget caps, and fires alerts before overages hit. BUILD: The factory scaffolds a simple intake form (API key + budget thresholds), a Claude-generated daily digest email, and a Stripe subscription link — no custom infra; the OpenAI usage API is public. SELL: Target engineering managers and CTOs via LinkedIn (filter: title 'Engineering Manager' OR 'CTO', company size 10–200, tech/agency sector) and relevant Slack communities (e.g., AI Tinkerers, agency ops groups); outreach batches go out only after Youval approves. MAINTAIN: Usage polling runs on a cron, Claude drafts and sends alert emails, Stripe handles billing — operator touch is approving outreach batches and reviewing the weekly anomaly log. ONLY recurring human step: approving outreach sends and any disputed charges.
notes: All build_gates pass: operational_autonomy=8 (≥7), buildability_with_ai=7 (≥6), buyer_clarity=8 (≥6), willingness_to_pay=7 (≥5). Defensibility is low (trivially copyable once OpenAI ships native controls), so the window is 6–12 months — validate pricing fast.
